draft.title: The adaptive immune response
card: The adaptive immune response targets one particular pathogen. It is slower to start than the innate response, but it is specific.
An antigen is a molecule, usually on the surface of a pathogen, that the immune system recognises. Each type of lymphocyte (white blood cell) responds to a particular antigen.
make antibodies, proteins that bind to a particular antigen. This marks the pathogen or stops it working.
some kill body cells that are infected. Others help, by signalling to other immune cells such as B cells.
draft.remember: Adaptive means targeted: B cells make antibodies, and T cells kill infected cells or help other immune cells.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the adaptive immune response differs from the innate response?
opts: It is slower to start but targets a particular antigen
It starts faster and responds the same way to all invaders
It is slower to start and treats all invaders the same way
It starts faster and targets a particular antigen
a.why: The adaptive response takes time to build up, but its cells and antibodies recognise one specific antigen. The innate response is the fast one that treats invaders alike, so the options describing speed or sameness the other way round are wrong.
a.clue: Think about both speed and how specific the response is.

b.q: A virus infects cells lining Tom's airways. Which immune cells would kill Tom's infected cells?
opts: T cells that kill infected cells
B cells, by making antibodies inside the cells
Antibodies, by engulfing the infected cells
B cells, by signalling to other immune cells
b.why: Some T cells kill body cells that are infected. B cells make antibodies, which are proteins that bind antigens, and antibodies are not cells that kill or engulf. Signalling to other immune cells is a helping role of T cells, not B cells.
b.clue: Which cell type has a killing role, and which makes proteins?

a.best: It is slower to start but targets a particular antigen

b.best: T cells that kill infected cells

problems.detail: The correct option repeats the stem's word 'kill' ('T cells that kill infected cells'), and no other option names a killing role. The clue also points straight to 'a killing role', so students can match words without knowing the idea.

'Each type of lymphocyte responds to a particular antigen' is loose. It reads as if B cells and T cells, the two types, each respond to one antigen. It is each lymphocyte (each clone) that is specific. Calling lymphocytes simply '(white blood cell)' also suggests they are the same thing, when lymphocytes are one kind of white blood cell.

proposal.title: The adaptive immune response
card: The adaptive immune response targets one particular pathogen. It is slower to start than the innate response, but it is specific.
An antigen is a molecule, usually on the surface of a pathogen, that the immune system recognises. Lymphocytes are one kind of white blood cell, and each lymphocyte recognises one particular antigen.
make antibodies, proteins that bind to a particular antigen. Antibodies work outside cells, such as in the blood, where they mark pathogens or stop them working.
some destroy body cells that are infected. Others help, by signalling to other immune cells such as B cells.
proposal.remember: Adaptive means targeted: B cells make antibodies, and T cells destroy infected cells or help other immune cells.

a.q: Which statement best describes how the adaptive immune response differs from the innate response?
opts: It is slower to start but targets a particular antigen
It starts faster and responds the same way to all invaders
It is slower to start and treats all invaders the same way
It starts faster and targets a particular antigen
a.why: The adaptive response takes time to build up, but each lymphocyte and antibody recognises one specific antigen. The innate response is the fast one that treats invaders alike, so options with speed or sameness the other way round are wrong.
a.clue: Think about both speed and how specific the response is.

b.q: A virus is inside cells lining Tom's airways. Which part of the adaptive response acts on those infected cells directly?
opts: T cells, by destroying the infected body cells
B cells, by destroying the infected body cells
Antibodies, by entering the infected body cells
T cells, by making antibodies against the virus
b.why: Some T cells destroy body cells that are infected. B cells make antibodies rather than destroying cells, and antibodies work outside cells, so they cannot reach a virus inside them. Making antibodies is the job of B cells, not T cells.
b.clue: Where do antibodies do their work, and which cells make them?
